decisions.reason: The product has remained visible for two years and is backed by a strong quantified customer outcome, so its performance appears above aspiration and gives little reason to reallocate resources away from it.

A dedicated product page in both 2023 and 2024 suggests the shredder is meeting at least acceptable aspirations for a mature machinery firm, even if public evidence is less explicit than for the modular plant concept.
The concept is supported by a named customer investment and a quantified savings case, which indicates satisfactory market validation and makes withdrawal unlikely.
As a 2024 launch in a product area close to the firm's core capabilities, it would likely be kept while management uses organisational slack to learn more before judging it a failure.

This 2024 launch is still in the early uncertainty phase, so although it faces a higher risk of review than older products, a conservative German machinery firm would usually continue it unless results clearly fall below aspiration.
